concept.title: Limitations of Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist

conbody.p: Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist may operate abnormally or unexpectedly under the following circumstances:

li.p: If the area around the rear-side radar is obstructed by the vehicle, a pillar, a wall, or other objects.
You are departing from areas with overgrown foliage.
You are departing from areas where roads are wet.
The speed of an approaching vehicle is fast or slow.
If the area around the rear-side radar is blocked when exiting simultaneously with an adjacent vehicle.

conbody.p: Braking control may not work, and your attention is required in the following circumstances:

li.p: The vehicle vibrates severely while you drive over a bumpy, uneven road or pothole.
You drive on a slippery surface such as snow, rain, ice, and so on.
The tire pressure is low or a tire is damaged.
Remote Smart Parking Assist is operating (if equipped).
If the brakes are modified.

note.p: For more information about the rear corner radar, refer to .

li.p: You are driving near a vehicle or structure
Structure

Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist may be limited when you drive near a vehicle or structure, and it may not detect a vehicle approaching from the left or right. The function may not warn you or control the brakes when necessary.
Always check your surroundings while backing up.
The vehicle is in a complex parking environment

Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist may detect vehicles that are parking or pulling out near your vehicle (for example, a vehicle leaving from beside your vehicle, a vehicle parking or pulling out behind your vehicle, a vehicle that is approaching your vehicle making a turn, and so on).
The function may unnecessarily warn you and control the brake.
Always check your surroundings while backing up.
The vehicle is parked diagonally

Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist may be limited when you back up diagonally and may not detect a vehicle approaching from the left or right. The function may not warn you or control the brakes when necessary.
Always check your surroundings while backing up.
The vehicle is on or near a slope

Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist may be limited when your vehicle is on or near an uphill or downhill slope, and it may not detect a vehicle approaching from the left or right. The function may not warn you or control the brakes when necessary.
Always check your surroundings while backing up.
You are pulling into a parking space where there is a structure
Structure
Wall

Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist may detect vehicles passing ahead of you when you park in reverse into a parking space with a wall or structure in the rear or side area. The function may unnecessarily warn you and control the brake.
Always check your surroundings while backing up.
The vehicle is parked backward
Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist may detect vehicles passing behind you when you park in a parking space in reverse. The function may unnecessarily warn you and control the brake.
Always check your surroundings while backing up.
When you are towing a trailer or another vehicle, turn OFF Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist for safety reasons.
Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist may not operate properly if there is strong electromagnetic interference.
Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist may not activate for 3 seconds after you start your vehicle or initialize the rear corner radars.
Even if you restart the vehicle with the sensors blocked or malfunctioning, Rear Cross-Traffic Collision-Avoidance Assist may not operate properly, as the function maintains its last setting.
